source.publisher: Northern Whig (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every name read from the page image; no contest after withdrawals, no poll

note: Triennial election of the rural district council, polled 28 May 1914: contests in Ballymartrim, Brootally, Clady, Glenaul and Middletown. Labels are printed only in the results of the contests. Returned unopposed. Robert Lyons withdrew (he was also nominated for Markethill). John Corkey: no party label printed in 1914. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Glenanne, 25 May 1905, printed 'Unionist': Armagh Guardian, 28 April 1905, p. 5 ("Guardians' Nominations"; "All the candidates are Unionists save where marked N."); withdrawals from the Armagh Guardian, 5 May 1905, p. 4 ("Poor Law Guardians": contests and withdrawals); Markethill, Armagh County Council, 29 May 1924, printed 'U': Lurgan Mail, 7 June 1924, p. 7 ("Co. Armagh Election Results"); nominations and labels from the Frontier Sentinel, 10 May 1924, p. 5). The name stands at elections from 1899 to 1939 and may be a father and son.
